query: Out of Uniform The next challenger steps in hooded, and drops the hood: Bram Hollis, without his red sash. He sees you and goes the colour of it. "You didn't see me," he says, fast and low. "I didn't see you. Nobody down here writes anything down. That's the point." Then, loud, for the crowd: "Well? Get in the chalk!" Fight him His ward finally gives, and he sits down hard in the chalk. Then something odd happens: he laughs, a real one, out loud. "Nobody's ever beaten me where my father couldn't hear about it," he says. He offers you his hand. He walks through your spells like rain and puts you on the flagstones. On the steps he stops. "Not a word," he says. "And not a demerit either. We were never here." Let him have the bout You step back out of the chalk and bow to him. He stares at you as if it were a trick. On the stairs to the dormitory next morning, your name isn't in his ledger, and he looks away first.
